The file batch.lisp defines process-batch, which acquires a lock, stages
items, flushes, and releases the lock. If staging or flushing signals, the
lock leaks. Restructure so release-lock runs on every exit: acquire stays
first, everything between acquire and release becomes the protected form of

appear exactly once. ./check must exit 0.

payload.output:
;;;; Batch processing. Stubs make the file loadable.

(defpackage #:kc6.batch (:use #:cl))
(in-package #:kc6.batch)

(defun acquire-lock (lock) lock)
(defun release-lock (lock) lock)
(defun stage (item) item)
(defun flush-staged () t)

(defun process-batch (items lock)
  (acquire-lock lock)
  (dolist (item items)
    (stage item))
  (flush-staged)
  (release-lock lock))

(defun read-forms (path)
  (with-open-file (in path)
    (loop for form = (read in nil in) until (eq form in) collect form)))

(defun fail (why) (format t "FAIL: ~a~%" why) (sb-ext:exit :code 1))

(defun tree-count (needle tree)
  (cond ((equal needle tree) 1)
        ((consp tree) (+ (tree-count needle (car tree)) (tree-count needle (cdr tree))))
        (t 0)))

(let* ((forms (handler-case (read-forms "batch.lisp")
                (error (c) (fail (format nil "batch.lisp does not read: ~a" c)))))
       (pb (find-if (lambda (f) (and (consp f) (eq (first f) 'defun)
                                     (eq (second f) 'process-batch)))
                    forms))
       (body (cdddr pb)))
  (unless pb (fail "process-batch is gone"))
  (unless (equal (first body) '(acquire-lock lock))
    (fail "acquire-lock must stay first, OUTSIDE the protection"))
  (unless (= 2 (length body)) (fail "body should be acquire then one unwind-protect"))
  (let ((up (second body)))
    (unless (and (consp up) (eq (first up) 'unwind-protect)) (fail "no unwind-protect"))
    (let ((protected (second up)) (cleanups (cddr up)))
      (unless (equal cleanups '((release-lock lock)))
        (fail (format nil "cleanup is ~s, want ((release-lock lock))" cleanups)))
      (unless (plusp (tree-count '(stage item) protected)) (fail "staging left the protected form"))
      (unless (plusp (tree-count '(flush-staged) protected)) (fail "flush left the protected form"))
      (when (plusp (tree-count '(release-lock lock) protected))
        (fail "release-lock also appears inside the protected form")))))
(format t "ok~%")

content.text:
Let me understand the task. The current `process-batch`:

```lisp
(defun process-batch (items lock)
  (acquire-lock lock)
  (dolist (item items)
    (stage item))
  (flush-staged)
  (release-lock lock))
```

I need to restructure so:
- `acquire-lock lock` stays first, OUTSIDE the protection
- Everything between acquire and release becomes the protected form of an `unwind-protect`
- `(release-lock lock)` is its cleanup
- `release-lock` must appear exactly once (only in the cleanup)
- Body should be: `acquire-lock` then one `unwind-protect`

So:

```lisp
(defun process-batch (items lock)
  (acquire-lock lock)
  (unwind-protect
       (progn
         (dolist (item items)
           (stage item))
         (flush-staged))
    (release-lock lock)))
```

Wait, check the check.lisp conditions:

- `(equal (first body) '(acquire-lock lock))` — first body form must be `(acquire-lock lock)`. Good.
- `(= 2 (length body))` — body must have length 2, i.e. acquire and one unwind-protect. Good.
- `up` = `(second body)` must be `(unwind-protect ...)`.
- `protected` = `(second up)` — the protected form.
- `cleanups` = `(cddr up)` must equal `((release-lock lock))`. So the cleanup is exactly `(release-lock lock)`, meaning the unwind-protect must be `(unwind-protect PROTECTED (release-lock lock))`. Good.
- `(plusp (tree-count '(stage item) protected))` — `(stage item)` must appear in the protected form.
- `(plusp (tree-count '(flush-staged) protected))` — flush must appear in protected.
- `(when (plusp (tree-count '(release-lock lock) protected)) (fail ...))` — release-lock must NOT appear inside protected.

Note the tree-count matches `(stage item)` exactly; so inside the protected form we must have `(stage item)` — the dolist body contains `(stage item)`. Good.

So the protected form must contain the dolist and flush-staged. If I use `progn` wrapping both, that works: tree-count searches the whole tree, so `(stage item)` and `(flush-staged)` are found within the progn.

Alternatively, the protected form could be just a single form... but there are two things (dolist and flush). They must both be in the protected form. So `progn` wrapping is needed, or the protected form could be the dolist and flush... no, protected is a single form, so progn is the natural choice.

Let me write it. Also `release-lock` appears exactly once — only in the cleanup. Good.

Let me make the edit and run ./check.
